name: CFPS Inhibitor Dose (Part 3a)
description: Part 3a of the TEM-1 inhibitor screen, sized to the purified-enzyme dose-response design in exp2_100ul_report.md: 5 compound rows (A-E, 4 concentrations x 2 duplicate wells each, compound preplated by hand before this run) plus a vehicle-control row (F1-F4, 2 duplicate pairs) -- 44 wells total, one robot run. Compound, vehicle, and (later) nitrocefin are all manual, off-robot; the robot's only job here is enzyme, dispensed from a fresh per-row aliquot tube in reagent_block. Each row keeps one tip for its whole span (source and volume are constant across a row's wells), and each duplicate pair shares a single aspirate: one draw of enzyme_total_vol_ul (2x enzyme_vol_ul) split into two equal dispenses, so the aliquot tube is only touched once per pair. The F5-F8 no-enzyme-blank wells get buffer by hand instead and have no nodes here. After the last row's enzyme is dispensed, the robot seals the plate and loads it into the shaker/incubator (lid closed) -- from there, starting and monitoring the incubation, adding nitrocefin by hand, and running cfps_inhibitor_kinetic_read (Part 3b) to load the reader are all manual.

nodes.label: Seal Plate
nodes.description: Grab the reaction plate short-side, seal it on the PlateMax (open door, load, pick + place seal, close door, press seal), unload it, and drop it back home.

nodes.label: Open Incubator Lid
nodes.description: Open the shaker/incubator lid before the arm reaches in -- never grab toward a machine that's still closed.

nodes.label: Re-grab Sealed Plate
nodes.description: Pick the sealed plate back up (short-side) to carry it to the incubator.

nodes.label: Load Plate Into Incubator
nodes.description: Place the sealed plate into the incubator slot and release it.

nodes.label: Close Incubator Lid (run ends here)
nodes.description: Final robot action. The sealed plate is left in the closed incubator -- starting/monitoring the incubation and retrieving the plate afterward (to add nitrocefin by hand) are manual from here.

nodes.label: Checkpoint: run started
nodes.description: Registers this execution in data/logs/ before any hardware moves, so a run that fails early is still visible to the tracker instead of leaving nothing behind. Its outgoing edge is deliberately 'default', not 'on_success': a checkpoint is bookkeeping, and a failure to record progress must never abort a run that is physically fine. The validator flags this as unconditional -- that is the intent.

nodes.label: Checkpoint: enzyme dispensing done
nodes.description: Refreshes the run folder once every row's enzyme dispensing is complete, before pipette stowing -- so a failure there still has every dispensed leg on record. Its outgoing edge is deliberately 'default', not 'on_success': a checkpoint is bookkeeping, and a failure to record progress must never abort a run that is physically fine. The validator flags this as unconditional -- that is the intent.
